name: Iran APT34 — Helix Kitten / DNSpionage
author: Threat Intelligence Team
prerequisites: DNS query logs with query type (A, TXT, CNAME, MX) available in SIEM
Passive DNS or DNS resolver log access for hunt window
Network flow data covering internal-to-internet communications
VPN and remote access authentication logs available
required_tools: Splunk or Elastic with DNS + proxy + VPN index
dnstwist or PassiveDNS for domain analysis

hunt_actions.title: DNS Tunneling and C2 via DNS (DNSpionage)
actions: Hunt for high-volume DNS TXT queries indicative of DNSpionage C2: `index=dns query_type=TXT | stats count as txt_count, dc(query) as unique_domains by src_ip | where txt_count > 50 | sort -txt_count` — DNSpionage uses DNS TXT records to pass commands; compare queried domains against Cisco Umbrella or Passive DNS for registration age and category

Detect DNS subdomain exfiltration (long encoded subdomains): In Zeek dns.log: `cat /path/to/dns.log | zeek-cut id.orig_h query | awk '{ split($2,a,"."); for(i in a) if(length(a[i])>20) print $0 }' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -30` — APT34 encodes stolen data in subdomain labels; labels > 20 chars are anomalous

hunt_actions.title: VALUEVAULT and LONGWATCH Credential Stealer Artifacts
actions: Hunt for VALUEVAULT execution (Windows Credential Manager dumper): `index=windows EventCode=4688 CommandLine=*vault* OR (CommandLine=*vaultcmd* AND CommandLine=*/list*) | table _time, host, SubjectUserName, CommandLine` — VALUEVAULT exports Windows Vault credentials to a file; also look for: `Get-ChildItem -Path $env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Vault\ -Recurse` access events in PowerShell logs

Detect LONGWATCH keylogger artifacts (writes to log files in temp directories): `index=windows EventCode=11 (TargetFilename=*\Temp\*.log OR TargetFilename=*\AppData\Local\Temp\*.dat) | stats count by host, TargetFilename | sort -count` (Sysmon File Create Event 11) — LONGWATCH logs keystrokes to a hidden file; any process repeatedly writing small amounts to a temp .log file is suspicious

hunt_actions.title: Living-off-the-Land and VBScript Abuse
actions: Hunt for APT34's PICKPOCKET and HYPERDRIVE VBScript/macro loaders: `index=windows EventCode=4688 (Image=*wscript.exe* OR Image=*cscript.exe*) ParentImage IN (*WINWORD.EXE*,*EXCEL.EXE*,*OUTLOOK.EXE*) | table _time, host, ParentImage, CommandLine` — VBScript droppers launching from Office are a primary APT34 delivery mechanism

Detect scheduled task creation used for persistence (APT34 pattern): `index=windows EventCode=4698 | rex field=TaskContent '<Command>(?P<cmd>[^<]+)' | where match(cmd, 'wscript|cscript|powershell|mshta|regsvr32') | table _time, host, TaskName, cmd, SubjectUserName`

hunt_actions.title: Exchange and OWA Credential Harvesting
actions: Hunt for suspicious OWA login patterns (APT34 targets Exchange for credential harvesting and email access): `index=exchange OR index=iis cs-uri-stem=*/owa/* sc-status=200 | stats dc(c-ip) as unique_ips, count as logins by cs-username | where unique_ips > 5 | sort -unique_ips` — a single account authenticating from many IPs to OWA indicates credential stuffing or account compromise

Detect Exchange web shell installation (APT34 deploys web shells to Exchange servers): `index=iis cs-uri-stem IN (*/owa/*,*/ews/*,*/autodiscover/*) sc-status=200 cs-method=POST | stats count by cs-uri-stem, c-ip | where count > 20 | sort -count` — POST requests to static Exchange paths are indicators; also run: `Get-ChildItem -Path 'C:\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\' -Recurse -Filter '*.aspx' | Where-Object { $_.CreationTime -gt (Get-Date).AddDays(-30) }`

questions: Is DNS query logging enabled on all internal resolvers and forwarded to the SIEM, including query type (TXT, MX, A, CNAME) and the full query string including all subdomain labels?
Is the organization's Exchange or Office 365 environment configured to block legacy authentication protocols (Basic Auth, NTLM to OWA), and is this verified in current sign-in logs?
Are external DNS resolvers restricted such that internal hosts can only query approved internal resolvers (no direct port 53 access to internet), enforced via firewall egress rules?
Are Outlook Web Access (OWA) and Exchange Web Services (EWS) endpoints protected by multi-factor authentication and monitored for authentication anomalies?
Is there a passive DNS or DNS history capability to identify recently registered domains mimicking the organization's name or those of its partners and supply chain?
Are VBScript and JScript execution via wscript.exe and cscript.exe blocked for standard user accounts via AppLocker or Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy?
Has the organization's Exchange server been assessed for web shell presence in the aspnet_client, OWA, and EWS directories within the last 90 days?
Are threat intelligence feeds specific to APT34/OilRig IOCs integrated into the SIEM, email gateway, and DNS filtering platform to enable automated detection?
